cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Approve the Harmless Version
cards.instruction: Get approval for a harmless version of your plan, then gradually reveal what that approval now commits them to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. May I put one extra chair in the hall?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Excellent. It's for the chair of my new tenants' committee.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I approved furniture, not a committee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then welcome to our first agenda item: what your chair authorises.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asks furniture permission despite prefixed authority; A3 reveals committee chair; A5 sets agenda but your chair confuses the approved object with B role.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 grants chair and B4 distinguishes furniture from committee; A5 agenda links to objection but its ownership shift is unclear.

relationship.evidence: B2 harmless assent and B4 correction are plausible building-use concerns.

heightening.evidence: A5 makes B4 scope objection a committee agenda, a useful escalation obscured by chair reference.

specificity.evidence: A1 hall chair clear; A3 committee head versus object pun and A5 your chair need reader repair.
